title: Spinal ligaments
summary: Quasi-static uniaxial tension of each lumbar and thoracic ligament (bone-ligament-bone): force vs elongation and nominal stress vs nominal strain to failure.
simulate: Isolate the ligament with its two bony attachments (bone-ligament-bone); remove all other structures.
Define L0 = attachment-to-attachment length at zero force (slack removed, <= 5 N preload) and A0 = undeformed cross-section.
Fix one bone; move the other along the ligament fibre direction at a quasi-static rate (no viscous or rate effects).
Report nominal stress F/A0 (MPa) against nominal strain dL/L0 (%) as one curve per ligament and region, up to failure.
Lumbar capsule equilibrium simulation: hold each strain 300 s and report the relaxed stress.

outputs.label: Stress at rupture
outputs.definition: Nominal stress F/A0 at rupture of the ligament in tension (MPa)

studies.sample: 132 lumbar ligaments (T12-S1), 38 cadavers; mean curves per level group (Fig 1)
studies.loading: Displacement control, in situ tension to failure at 10 mm/s (Myklebust 1988 protocol); no preload stated; lumbar T12-S1 ALL, PLL, LF, ISL, SSL, capsule

studies.sample: 43 whole ligaments, 18 spines (34 cadaveric, 9 surgical ISL+SSL); 1 mm/min
studies.loading: Displacement control, tension at 1 mm/min to rupture (with load-unload cycles); no preload stated; whole ligaments with bony ends, T1-S1 (ALL, PLL, LF, ISL+SSL)
Tension at strain rate ~0.33/min: 5 cycles to 1 kg then 2 kg (~10/20 N), relaxation tests, then to rupture; 37 °C Ringer; L3-L4 ligamenta flava

studies.sample: 25 lumbar facet capsules (L1-S1) tested parallel to fibres, 8 spines; equilibrium (300 s) stress
studies.loading: Displacement control, ramp-hold to 10-50% grip strain at 15%/s, 300 s hold (equilibrium); 0.1 N preload; 6 preconditioning cycles to 50%; lumbar facet capsules

studies.sample: same 100 thoracic samples as Wolny 2024; nominal stress F/A0 vs stretch
studies.loading: Displacement control, tension at 0.5/s to rupture; 5 N preload; 60 precond. cycles at 10% strain, 1 Hz; 36.6 °C; thoracic bone-ligament-bone, T1-T12

notes: Definitions (nominal): strain = (L - L0)/L0 with L0 the zero-force length between bony attachments; stress = F/A0 with A0 the undeformed cross-section. Taken from the user's AF work: Ghezelbash et al. 2021 Acta Biomater preprint (SSRN 3677348) p. 20, Fig. 4 caption "nominal strain = applied displacement/initial length; nominal stress = applied force/initial area" (Fig. 5: small preload to remove slack); Ghezelbash 2020 J Biomech 102:109463 p. 4 reports nominal stress-strain. None of the user's papers defines ligament strain itself (U11 bioRxiv 2025 p. 18 lists ligaments only as "nonlinear stress-strain curves"). Source variants: Wiczenbach P11 = F/A0, lambda - 1 (identical); Chazal smallest CSA, length between nearest insertions; Nachemson in situ resting length; Little optical first-principal strain.

Quasi-static only. Rates: Chazal 1 mm/min; Nachemson ~0.33 %/min; Neumann 2.5 mm/s (~1 %/s); Wolny/Wiczenbach 0.5 /s (called quasi-static by the authors); Pintar rate not stated; its mechanics data are Myklebust 1988's, pulled at 1 cm/s (Myklebust 1988 p. 526), i.e. not quasi-static; Little equilibrium stress after 300 s hold. Dropped: Little peak (viscous) curve and dynamic moduli; Hindle 1990 (force vs flexion angle, incl. 12.5 deg/s); Tkaczuk 1968 and Iida 2002 (no elongation or strain); Myklebust 1988 (failure force/deflection only, 1 cm/s); all single-value stiffness/modulus rows.

Stress-strain only (nominal stress = F/A0, nominal strain = dL/L0). Pintar 1992 force-deformation curves are converted with Pintar's own mean CSA and length; force-elongation data of Chazal 1985, Wolny 2024 and Neumann 1992 stay in bench/tests.
agent_prompt: You are given a model of the human lumbar and thoracic spinal ligaments. Run the 13 simulations in `simulations`, one per ligament and region (lumbar or thoracic): isolate the ligament as a bone-ligament-bone unit, set L0 at zero force and A0 = undeformed cross-section, pull along the fibres quasi-statically to failure and report nominal stress F/A0 (MPa) against nominal strain (L - L0)/L0 (%). The lumbar capsule equilibrium simulation reports the relaxed stress after 300 s holds at each strain. Use one parameter set per ligament and region; end your curve at failure. Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
